subject: biology
title: Microscopy
apparatus: light microscope; slide; coverslip; specimen; stain; forceps; mounted needle
dependentVariable: visible cell structures and measured image size
controlVariables: same microscope calibration; same staining approach when comparing
methodOverview: Place a thin specimen on a slide, add an appropriate stain, lower a coverslip at an angle, begin with the lowest-power objective, focus, then increase magnification. Produce a clear biological drawing with labels and a scale or magnification.
accuracyReliability: Use the lowest power to locate cells; fine focus at high power; measure with a calibrated scale; keep image and real size in the same units.
safety: Handle glass slides and stains carefully; use forceps or a mounted needle rather than fingers.
scientificRationale: A thin specimen lets light pass through; stain increases contrast; lowering the coverslip at an angle reduces trapped air bubbles.
expectedPattern: Higher magnification reveals more detail but gives a smaller field of view.
dataGraphFocus: Image size or scale-bar calculation; compare observable structures without inventing unseen detail.
commonError: A thick or folded specimen produces overlapping, poorly focused cells.
improvement: Use a thinner single-cell layer, repeat measurements across several cells and calibrate the scale.

subject: biology
title: Microbiology: antibiotics and antiseptics
apparatus: sterile agar plate; bacterial culture; sterile swab; forceps; paper discs; disinfectants/antibiotics; tape; incubator; ruler
dependentVariable: diameter or area of zone of inhibition
controlVariables: bacterial species; agar depth; disc size; volume/concentration; incubation time and temperature
methodOverview: Use aseptic technique to spread bacteria evenly on sterile agar. Add equally sized antimicrobial discs with sterile forceps, include a sterile-water control, tape the lid at a few points, incubate inverted at 25°C in school laboratories, then measure inhibition zones without opening.
accuracyReliability: Use equal discs and antimicrobial volumes; measure two perpendicular diameters; repeat plates; compare mean zone area.
safety: Disinfect benches, minimise lid opening, use sterile equipment, tape but do not fully seal, incubate at 25°C and do not reopen grown plates.
scientificRationale: Aseptic technique prevents contamination; inverted incubation stops condensation dripping; 25°C reduces growth of harmful human pathogens; a control shows whether the solvent/disc affects growth.
expectedPattern: A more effective antimicrobial produces a larger clear zone, provided diffusion conditions are comparable.
dataGraphFocus: Compare mean diameter or area; identify anomalies; avoid claiming the treatment killed bacteria when it may only inhibit growth.
commonError: Unequal bacterial lawns or discs placed too close cause overlapping zones.
improvement: Use a standardised inoculum, equal spreading, larger plates or fewer well-spaced discs and repeat.

subject: biology
title: Osmosis in plant tissue
apparatus: potato cylinders; cork borer; ruler; balance; labelled tubes; sugar/salt solutions; paper towel; timer
dependentVariable: change or percentage change in tissue mass
controlVariables: initial cylinder dimensions; tissue source; solution volume; time; temperature; blotting method
methodOverview: Cut equal potato cylinders, measure initial mass, place each in a different known concentration for the same time, remove, blot in a standard way and reweigh. Calculate percentage mass change and plot against concentration.
accuracyReliability: Use a cork borer and equal lengths; zero a precise balance; blot consistently; use repeats and calculate means.
safety: Cut away from fingers and handle glassware/solutions carefully.
scientificRationale: Water moves through partially permeable cell membranes from higher water concentration to lower water concentration. Blotting removes surface liquid so only tissue mass is measured.
expectedPattern: Dilute solution usually causes mass gain; concentrated solution causes mass loss; zero percentage change estimates the isotonic concentration.
dataGraphFocus: Plot concentration on x-axis and percentage mass change on y-axis; draw a best-fit line/curve and interpolate the x-intercept.
commonError: Cylinders with different surface-area-to-volume ratios change mass at different rates.
improvement: Use the same cork borer and length, take tissue from the same potato, repeat each concentration and use more concentrations near the x-intercept.

subject: biology
title: Food tests
apparatus: food samples; test tubes; pipettes; Benedict’s solution; iodine solution; Biuret reagent; ethanol; water bath
independentVariable: food sample or known nutrient concentration
controlVariables: sample volume; reagent volume; heating time and temperature
methodOverview: Prepare a food solution. For reducing sugar add Benedict’s and heat in a water bath; for starch add iodine; for protein add Biuret reagent; for lipid use the ethanol emulsion test where appropriate. Record the positive observation and use known controls.
accuracyReliability: Use equal volumes, clean labelled apparatus, a thermostatically controlled water bath and positive/negative controls; repeat borderline results.
safety: Wear eye protection; use a water bath for Benedict’s; keep flammable ethanol away from flames.
scientificRationale: Controls confirm reagents work and show the negative colour; crushing/dissolving exposes molecules; the water bath heats samples safely and evenly.
expectedPattern: Benedict’s: blue to green/yellow/orange/brick-red; iodine: orange-brown to blue-black; Biuret: blue to lilac/purple; lipid emulsion: cloudy white.
dataGraphFocus: Present a results table with sample, starting colour, final observation and inference; do not treat qualitative colour as an exact concentration without calibration.
commonError: Cross-contamination between droppers creates false positives.
improvement: Use separate clean pipettes, rinse glassware, label tubes and include known positive and negative controls.

subject: biology
title: Effect of pH on amylase
apparatus: amylase; starch; buffer solutions; iodine; spotting tile; pipettes; water bath; timer
dependentVariable: time for starch to disappear or rate = 1/time
controlVariables: amylase and starch concentration/volume; temperature; sampling interval; total volume
methodOverview: Equilibrate amylase, starch and buffer at constant temperature. Mix amylase with buffer, add starch and start timing. Every 30 s place a sample onto iodine. Record when iodine remains orange-brown, repeat across pH values and calculate rate.
accuracyReliability: Use buffer solutions, a water bath, equal volumes/concentrations, fixed sampling intervals and repeats; use separate pipettes.
safety: Wear eye protection; iodine is an irritant and stains; use a water bath rather than direct flame.
scientificRationale: Buffer keeps pH constant; iodine detects remaining starch; constant temperature prevents it becoming a confounding variable.
expectedPattern: Rate rises toward an optimum pH then falls as active-site shape/charge becomes less suitable or the enzyme denatures.
dataGraphFocus: Plot pH against rate (1/time), not time, if comparing reaction rate; draw a smooth best-fit curve.
commonError: The true endpoint occurs between 30 s samples, creating timing uncertainty.
improvement: Sample more frequently near the endpoint or use a colorimeter/data logger for a continuous objective measure.

subject: biology
title: Rate of photosynthesis
apparatus: pondweed; lamp/LED; ruler; sodium hydrogencarbonate solution; thermometer; stopwatch; gas syringe/capillary
independentVariable: light intensity or distance from lamp
dependentVariable: oxygen bubbles per minute or oxygen volume per time
controlVariables: temperature; carbon dioxide concentration; pondweed length/species; wavelength; measurement time
methodOverview: Place pondweed in sodium hydrogencarbonate solution, allow it to acclimatise, set a measured lamp distance, record oxygen production for a fixed time, repeat and calculate a mean. Test several distances and control temperature.
accuracyReliability: Measure oxygen volume rather than variable bubble size where possible; use repeats; measure distance from lamp to pondweed; shield external light.
safety: Keep water away from electrical equipment; lamp may become hot; use an LED or heat shield.
scientificRationale: Sodium hydrogencarbonate supplies carbon dioxide; acclimatisation allows the rate to stabilise; temperature must be controlled because photosynthesis is enzyme-controlled.
expectedPattern: Rate increases with light intensity until another factor becomes limiting; intensity is approximately proportional to 1/distance².
dataGraphFocus: Plot light intensity (or 1/d²) against mean rate; identify plateau and anomalies.
commonError: Bubble counting is unreliable because bubble sizes vary and some oxygen dissolves.
improvement: Collect oxygen with a gas syringe/capillary, repeat, control temperature and use a range of intensities.

subject: biology
title: Reaction time
apparatus: metre ruler; chair/table; calculator; optional caffeine condition
independentVariable: condition such as caffeine, distraction or practice
dependentVariable: ruler distance fallen converted to reaction time
controlVariables: same participant where possible; same hand; ruler position; warning; environment; trial spacing
methodOverview: Participant rests forearm and places fingers at the zero mark. Release the ruler without warning; record catch distance. Repeat, calculate mean and convert distance to reaction time using a table or equation. Compare controlled conditions ethically.
accuracyReliability: Use many repeats, discard only justified anomalies, randomise condition order and use the same participant or a large matched sample.
safety: Keep the area clear; avoid unsafe doses of caffeine; obtain consent and allow withdrawal.
scientificRationale: No warning prevents anticipation; repeats reduce random error; random order reduces practice/fatigue bias.
expectedPattern: Shorter catch distance means shorter reaction time; distraction, tiredness, alcohol and some drugs usually slow responses.
dataGraphFocus: Plot participant means or compare distributions; a bar chart may suit categories, while scatter graphs suit continuous variables.
commonError: Practice improves performance across trials and can be mistaken for the treatment effect.
improvement: Use randomised/counterbalanced order, practice trials before data collection and sufficient participants.

subject: biology
title: Plant responses
apparatus: germinating seedlings; Petri dishes; cotton wool; light box; clinostat or directional light; ruler/protractor
controlVariables: seedling species/age; water; temperature; time; initial orientation; light intensity except direction
methodOverview: Place similar seedlings in controlled containers. Expose groups to directional light, uniform light/darkness or altered gravity orientation. Measure growth angle/length after a fixed time and compare controls.
accuracyReliability: Use many seedlings, random allocation, consistent starting orientation and objective angle measurements from photographs.
safety: Handle seedlings and glassware carefully; wash hands after biological material.
scientificRationale: A control distinguishes directional response from normal growth; rotating a clinostat averages the gravity stimulus; auxin redistribution changes cell elongation.
expectedPattern: Shoots are positively phototropic and negatively gravitropic; roots are usually positively gravitropic.
dataGraphFocus: Plot mean angle or growth with spread/error bars; compare direction and magnitude, not only final length.
commonError: Seedlings vary naturally and may begin at different angles.
improvement: Use a larger sample, random allocation, measure initial and final angle, photograph from a fixed position and blind the measurer.

subject: biology
title: Field investigation
apparatus: quadrats; transect tape; random-number generator; identification key; ruler; abiotic sensors
independentVariable: distance along gradient or environmental factor
dependentVariable: abundance, frequency or distribution of organisms
controlVariables: quadrat size; sampling effort; season/time; identification method; observer; measurement method
methodOverview: For abundance in an area, generate random coordinates and place quadrats without bias. For a gradient, place quadrats at regular intervals along a transect. Identify species, count/estimate abundance, measure the abiotic factor and repeat sufficiently.
accuracyReliability: Use many samples, random coordinates, consistent quadrat size, a key, percentage cover rules and calibrated sensors.
safety: Assess terrain/weather; avoid harmful organisms; minimise habitat damage and replace moved objects.
scientificRationale: Random sampling reduces selection bias; systematic transects reveal change along a gradient; repeats improve representation.
expectedPattern: Distribution may correlate with an abiotic factor, but correlation alone does not prove causation.
dataGraphFocus: Use scatter graphs for abundance against a continuous factor; calculate means/frequency and describe correlation with anomalies.
commonError: Clumped distribution makes a small sample unrepresentative.
improvement: Increase number of randomly positioned quadrats, stratify the area if habitats differ and report uncertainty/range.

subject: biology
title: Decay of biological material
apparatus: milk or organic material; lipase/microorganisms; pH indicator/probe; water baths; timer; thermometers
dependentVariable: time for colour/pH change or rate of decay
controlVariables: sample volume; starting pH; organism/enzyme concentration; oxygen; measurement endpoint
methodOverview: Place equal samples at different controlled temperatures, add the same decomposer/enzyme source, start timing and measure pH or indicator change to a fixed endpoint. Repeat and calculate rate.
accuracyReliability: Use thermostatic water baths, objective pH probe, equal inoculum, sterile/clean technique where needed and repeats.
safety: Use school-safe organisms/materials; wear eye protection; avoid opening incubated cultures; wash hands.
scientificRationale: Temperature affects enzyme-controlled reactions in decomposers; a fixed endpoint permits fair timing; pH change can indicate product formation.
expectedPattern: Rate increases toward an optimum then falls if enzymes denature or organisms are harmed.
dataGraphFocus: Plot temperature against rate = 1/time; identify optimum and explain both sides of curve.
commonError: Water-bath temperature may change after cold samples are added.
improvement: Allow equilibration, monitor sample temperature with probes, use small equal samples and repeat.
